avoid: Throwing or kicking sand outside the dance box
children.counts: Even 4-count rhythms: slide right (1), slide left (2), shuffle right (3), shuffle left (4).
children.game_version: Play 'The Water Glass Statue': dancers balance a light paper cup or beanbag on their heads while competing to make the clearest swishing sounds in the sand without letting the item drop.

seniors.seated_version: Perform seated on a sturdy chair with feet resting on a sand-strewn wooden board, executing gentle forward and backward sliding shuffles from the ankles while maintaining an upright, supported spine.
seniors.standing_version: Hold lightly onto a barre or high chair back for stability while executing low sliding scrapes within a small boundary.
seniors.tempo_and_range: Reduce tempo to a slow, deliberate cadence; keep the foot excursions within 6 to 10 inches.

feedback_rules.description: Flag excessive torso sway, vertical bouncing, or head tilt as an error, distinguishing it from intentional lower-leg ankle articulation.
Detect lifting of the feet off the floor, which breaches the foundational rule that the dancer's feet never leave the ground.

learning_units.description: Maintain complete upper-body immobility from the hips up while executing percussive foot movements, keeping the head level enough to balance a glass of water.
Execute rhythmic swishing shuffles strictly from the ankles down without allowing the soles of the feet to leave the floor.
Confine all foot movement, sliding, and shuffling patterns entirely within a compact two-foot square zone.

prerequisites.description: Fine ankle articulation and the ability to maintain pelvic and spinal stability without torso sway.

social_formats.description: Solo theatrical specialty exhibition performed inside a compact sand box or small defined area on stage.
Stage trio ensemble performing coordinated sliding routines across a sand-strewn stage.

movement_profile.footwork: Rhythmic, swishing slides and shuffles executed from the ankles down with the soles never leaving the ground.
movement_profile.formation_and_space: Confined to a limited area of a few feet, such as a two-foot square zone or a designated wooden sand box.
movement_profile.levels_and_jumps: Strictly grounded; feet never leave the ground, with no aerial leaps or jumps.
movement_profile.partnering: Solo performance; historically also performed as an ensemble trio across a stage.
movement_profile.posture: Completely immobile and upright from the hips up, steady enough to balance a glass of water on the head.

signature_moves.description: A close-to-the-floor sliding shuffle where the sole skims across scattered sand to produce a rhythmic hiss.
signature_moves.name: swishing shuffle

signature_moves.description: Stationary percussive shuffling and sliding entirely confined within a two-foot square area.
signature_moves.name: two-foot box slide

movement_profile.what_to_avoid: Do not bounce, tilt, or swing the torso or hips; avoid lifting the feet off the floor.

music_profile.rhythm_pattern: Heavy syncopation over a 2/2 schottische framework.
music_profile.sound_description: A textured, rhythmic scraping sound characterized by the whispering hiss of leather soles, patent leather, or metal taps sliding through loose grains of sand against a resonant wooden board, punctuated by syncopated schottische pulses.

basic_steps: Scatter fine sand evenly across a small wooden board or low-sided wooden box.
Assume an upright posture with knees slightly softened and upper torso held completely motionless from the hips up.
Execute a forward sliding brush with the ball of one foot, scraping the sand against the wood.
Execute a backward dragging shuffle without lifting the sole entirely from the floor.
Alternate sliding strokes between feet in syncopated 2/2 meter, keeping all action confined from the ankles down within a two-foot square.
teaching.formation: Solo dancer in a confined wooden box or marked sand zone.
teaching.level_notes: Focus entirely on keeping the upper body motionless while generating clean friction sounds with the soles.
